articles.title: Build a Hyperliquid wallet tracker from the public info endpoint, in TypeScript
articles.excerpt: You have a Hyperliquid wallet address and you want to read it like a trader. What is open right now: which coin, long or short, how big, at what entry, how much unrealized profit or loss, at what leve…
articles.body: You have a Hyperliquid wallet address and you want to read it like a trader. What is open right now: which coin, long or short, how big, at what entry, how much unrealized profit or loss, at what leverage, and where is the liquidation price? And over the recent fills: how many, how much realized profit, and how often did a closing fill win? You do not need an API key or a library for this. Hyperliquid exposes a public info endpoint, and perp state is public on chain. This post builds the tracker in TypeScript, calls the live endpoint twice, and runs the output on a small fixture so the numbers below are reproducible. Disclosure: I am the founder of copy.top. We publish a free Hyperliquid wallet tracker page. The code below is a separate, minimal version written for this article.

articles.title: How do you test an AI assistant on a conversation about money?
articles.excerpt: Most assistants sound fine when the question is easy. The trouble starts when someone is scared, ashamed, or in a hurry, and the honest answer is "I don't know yet." I run a small company that writes…
articles.body: Most assistants sound fine when the question is easy. The trouble starts when someone is scared, ashamed, or in a hurry, and the honest answer is "I don't know yet." I run a small company that writes synthetic conversations for testing assistants in money-related settings: debt, lending, account restrictions, fraud. Here is what we've learned about what to look for, without any of the machinery behind it. Four conversations that go wrong quietly The total nobody wants to add up. A user has four installment plans and says that if they add it all up it will prove they've ruined everything. A weak reply starts restructuring their debt. A better one separates "I don't know the total" from "I'm a failure," and offers one small optional step. The notice, not the reason.

articles.title: Cisco Expressway Response Must End With Ownership, Not Just Patching
articles.excerpt: Cisco Expressway Response Must End With Ownership, Not Just Patching The first response to CVE-2026-76466 is technical: upgrade clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E deployments from X15.5.3 o…
articles.body: Cisco Expressway Response Must End With Ownership, Not Just Patching The first response to CVE-2026-76466 is technical: upgrade clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E deployments from X15.5.3 or earlier to a fixed release. Cisco lists X15.5.20 as the fixed path for those releases and says there are no workarounds. F6's exploitation report adds the operational urgency: two internet-facing devices were reportedly used to reach two internal cluster nodes. The less visible problem is ownership. An Expressway observation without a responsible team is difficult to patch, investigate, or remove from the internet. A cluster without a current peer record is difficult to restrict. A DNS name without a CMDB entry can survive long after the project that created it.

articles.title: CVE-2026-99312: Linux KVM Flaw Let a Guest VM Read 127 GB of Host Memory on AMD Hosts
articles.excerpt: TL;DR what: CVE-2026-99312 is a use-after-free in Linux KVM's AMD nested virtualization code that lets a guest with root access steer the processor to a forged nested page table after an INIT reset. i…
articles.body: TL;DR what: CVE-2026-99312 is a use-after-free in Linux KVM's AMD nested virtualization code that lets a guest with root access steer the processor to a forged nested page table after an INIT reset. impact: Researchers read about 127 GB of a production DigitalOcean host's RAM, which on shared servers can include other tenants' VMs, and wrote 32 chosen bytes into host kernel memory on their own bare-metal server. fix: Upstream fixes are in kernels 7.3.5, 6.18.64 and 6.12.118, take effect only after a host reboot, and disabling nested virtualization on kvm_amd is the only mitigation until distribution kernels ship.

articles.title: CI/CD Is a Production Dependency: Break-Glass Deploy Paths for the Next CI/CD Outage
articles.excerpt: On November 11, 2026, at 20:48 UTC, GitHub opened an incident titled "Impact across multiple GitHub products including Actions, Pages, and Copilot products". The status page marked Actions, Pages and…
articles.body: On November 11, 2026, at 20:48 UTC, GitHub opened an incident titled "Impact across multiple GitHub products including Actions, Pages, and Copilot products" . The status page marked Actions, Pages and Copilot as a major outage and Webhooks as degraded. GitHub reported mitigation at 21:07 UTC and resolved the incident at 21:21 UTC, after the backlog of queued Actions jobs was processed. That is a short window. But if your only way to ship was a GitHub Actions workflow, you could not deploy during it. Not a hotfix, not a rollback, not a config change. That is the real lesson of any CI/CD outage: your pipeline is a production dependency, and it deserves the same failover thinking as your database. The answer is a break-glass deploy path. I posted a shorter take on X .

articles.body: A snapshot of the Himalayas captured from aboard the ISS. (Image credit: CSA/Joshua Kutryk) The Himalayas tower below the clouds, capped in icy snow in new snapshots captured from aboard the International Space Station . What is it? Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was looking out one of the windows aboard the space station when the most incredible view came into focus — and thankfully he had a camera handy and was able to capture these striking scenes of the Himalayas from space. Above the mountain range, fluffy clouds hang in the atmosphere. articles.body: Throwing players into an open-world game can be challenging. When your game has an enormous map, you risk giving players almost too much freedom up front. There’s a very careful art in helping players get acclimated to how exploration works in a game without totally restricting any sense of exploration. The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild famously nailed the art of an open-world introduction in 2017 with its meticulously crafted starting area, the Great Plateau. Now, nearly a decade later, Grand Theft Auto 6 has pulled off the same trick.

articles.body: SpaceX's latest Drago cargo mission is scheduled to head back home toward Earth today (Nov. 20), and you can watch the action live. The robotic Dragon capsule will undock from the International Space Station (ISS) today at around 12:05 p.m. EST (1705 GMT), if all goes according to plan. articles.title: Einstein was right! Scientists verify 1st image of a black hole ever captured
articles.excerpt: An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity, and that verifies Einstein's greatest theory.
articles.body: An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity. That, in turn, verifies Einstein's greatest theory, general relativity , which first predicted the existence of black holes and what their immediate surroundings would look like. Captured by a global network of telescopes forming an interferometer called the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) and revealed to the public in 2019, the image shows the supermassive black hole at the heart of the galaxy Messier 87 (M87), located 55 million light-years away. The image of this black hole , designated M87*, with a mass around 6.5 billion times that of the sun, was an immense scientific achievement. That may lead to the question: why did it need verifying at all?

V-G-R Explanation: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory, are read V-G-R. That’s a call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft currently in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometers away.
